+"""Per-provider endpoint policy on the cheval Python path (cycle-129 FR-7, SDD D-7.2, D-8.0).
+
+The rule, applied at config load to every HTTP provider in the merged ``hounfour.providers`` view:
+
+* ``allow_insecure_endpoint`` is a host STRING, never a boolean. It must be an IP literal or ``localhost``
+  (an insecure endpoint is never resolved through DNS, so there is no rebinding), and the address must be
+  loopback (``127.0.0.0/8``, ``::1``) or RFC1918 (``10/8``, ``172.16/12``, ``192.168/16``). Link-local,
+  the cloud metadata addresses, unique-local IPv6 and every public range are refused.
+* An ``http://`` endpoint is admitted only when its host equals the provider's opt-in host. A mismatched
+  host, a public ``http`` host or an ``http`` endpoint without an opt-in fails at load with a named reason.
+* Every other endpoint keeps the cycle-099 refusals: ``https`` only, no userinfo, no control bytes or path
+  traversal, and no loopback, private, link-local, metadata or otherwise blocked IP literal (``localhost``
+  included). One provider's opt-in never changes another provider's checks.
+* ``keyless: true`` marks a provider that needs no credential; a literal ``auth: "local"`` is accepted and
+  normalised to ``keyless: true`` in the merged view. A keyless provider is admitted only when every model
+  declares ``context_window`` and ``dispatch_group``.
+
+ONE implementation: every URL and opt-in decision here is made by the canonical
+``.claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py`` (the module the bash callers and the health probe use),
+loaded by path as ``loa_cheval.codegen.emit_endpoint_validator_ts`` does: ``check_insecure_optin`` for the
+opt-in and ``validate_declared_endpoint`` (the full pipeline minus the host allowlist, which an
+operator-declared https host is not on) for the endpoint. The refusal codes are therefore the validator's
+codes, and URL parsing stays confined to that module (the cycle-099 import guard).
+``tests/test_endpoint_validator_optin.py`` runs one case table through both entry points.
+
+Request-time half (``TransportPolicy`` in ``providers/base.py``): for an opted-in provider, or a model whose
+``dispatch_group`` is ``local``, the adapter ignores proxy environment variables, refuses HTTP redirects and
+requires every request URL to stay under the declared endpoint path.
+
+CLI (used by ``model-health-probe.sh --provider <name>``; reads the merged config, never prints a secret)::
+
+    python3 -m loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy list-providers [--project-root DIR]
+    python3 -m loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy describe-provider NAME [--project-root DIR]
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+import threading
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+from loa_cheval.types import ConfigError
+
+# The literal auth values normalised to keyless (D-8.0). Only "local": any other literal could be a real key.
+KEYLESS_AUTH_LITERALS = frozenset({"local"})
+
+# .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py → .claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py
+_VALIDATOR_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "scripts" / "lib" / "endpoint-validator.py"
+_VALIDATOR: Any = None
+_VALIDATOR_LOCK = threading.Lock()
+
+
+def _validator() -> Any:
+    """The canonical endpoint-validator module, loaded once by path. A missing
+    or unloadable validator is a ConfigError (fail-closed: no endpoint is
+    admitted unchecked)."""
+    global _VALIDATOR
+    with _VALIDATOR_LOCK:
+        if _VALIDATOR is not None:
+            return _VALIDATOR
+        name = "loa_endpoint_validator_canonical"
+        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, _VALIDATOR_PATH)
+        if spec is None or spec.loader is None or not _VALIDATOR_PATH.is_file():
+            raise ConfigError(f"[ENDPOINT-VALIDATOR-MISSING] {_VALIDATOR_PATH} not found; reinstall the framework")
+        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+        sys.modules[name] = module
+        try:
+            spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — any load failure is fail-closed
+            sys.modules.pop(name, None)
+            raise ConfigError(f"[ENDPOINT-VALIDATOR-MISSING] {_VALIDATOR_PATH} failed to load: {exc}") from exc
+        _VALIDATOR = module
+        return module
+
+
+class EndpointPolicyError(ConfigError):
+    """A provider endpoint or opt-in refused at load. ``policy_code`` is the endpoint-validator code."""
+
+    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str, provider: Optional[str] = None):
+        where = f"providers.{provider}: " if provider else ""
+        super().__init__(f"[{code}] {where}{detail}", context={"policy_code": code, "provider": provider})
+        self.policy_code = code
+        self.detail = detail
+
+
+def split_url(url: str) -> Tuple[str, str, Optional[int], str]:
+    """(scheme, canonical host, explicit port or None, path) via the canonical validator; ValueError on a bad URL."""
+    return _validator().split_url(url)
+
+
+def canonical_optin_host(value: Any, provider: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
+    """Validate an ``allow_insecure_endpoint`` value and return its canonical host, or raise."""
+    ok, code, detail, host = _validator().check_insecure_optin(value)
+    if not ok:
+        raise EndpointPolicyError(code or "ENDPOINT-OPTIN-INVALID", detail or "invalid opt-in", provider)
+    return host
+
+
+def check_endpoint(endpoint: str, allow_insecure_endpoint: Any = None, provider: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Apply the D-7.2 rule to one provider's endpoint. Returns the canonical opt-in host (or None); raises."""
+    optin = canonical_optin_host(allow_insecure_endpoint, provider) if allow_insecure_endpoint is not None else None
+    result = _validator().validate_declared_endpoint(endpoint, allow_insecure_endpoint=optin)
+    if not result.valid:
+        raise EndpointPolicyError(result.code or "ENDPOINT-INVALID", result.detail or "endpoint refused", provider)
+    return optin
+
+
+# --- the merged view --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _is_cli_provider(prov: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    ptype = str(prov.get("type") or "")
+    if ptype.endswith("-headless"):
+        return True
+    models = prov.get("models") or {}
+    return bool(models) and isinstance(models, dict) and all(
+        isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("kind") == "cli" for m in models.values()
+    )
+
+
+def normalise_keyless(merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Pre-interpolation step: a literal ``auth: "local"`` becomes ``keyless: true`` (D-8.0); ``keyless`` must be a bool."""
+    providers = merged.get("providers")
+    if not isinstance(providers, dict):
+        return
+    for name, prov in providers.items():
+        if not isinstance(prov, dict):
+            continue
+        if "keyless" in prov and not isinstance(prov["keyless"], bool):
+            raise ConfigError(
+                f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.keyless must be true or false, got {prov['keyless']!r}"
+            )
+        auth = prov.get("auth")
+        if isinstance(auth, str) and auth.strip().lower() in KEYLESS_AUTH_LITERALS:
+            prov["keyless"] = True
+
+
+def validate_providers(merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Post-interpolation step: endpoint rule and keyless preconditions for every provider."""
+    providers = merged.get("providers")
+    if not isinstance(providers, dict):
+        return
+    for name, prov in providers.items():
+        if not isinstance(prov, dict):
+            continue
+        optin = prov.get("allow_insecure_endpoint")
+        endpoint = prov.get("endpoint")
+        if not _is_cli_provider(prov) and endpoint not in (None, ""):
+            if not isinstance(endpoint, str):
+                raise ConfigError(f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.endpoint must be a string")
+            check_endpoint(endpoint, optin, name)
+        elif optin is not None:
+            # An opt-in with nothing to apply to is still validated, so a typo never sits silent.
+            canonical_optin_host(optin, name)
+        if prov.get("keyless") is True:
+            models = prov.get("models") or {}
+            if not isinstance(models, dict) or not models:
+                raise ConfigError(f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name} is keyless but declares no models")
+            for model_id, model in models.items():
+                model = model if isinstance(model, dict) else {}
+                cw = model.get("context_window")
+                if not isinstance(cw, int) or isinstance(cw, bool) or cw <= 0:
+                    raise ConfigError(
+                        f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.models.{model_id}: a keyless provider is admitted only "
+                        f"with a declared context_window (a positive integer)"
+                    )
+                if not model.get("dispatch_group"):
+                    raise ConfigError(
+                        f"[CONFIG-INVALID] providers.{name}.models.{model_id}: a keyless provider is admitted only "
+                        f"with a declared dispatch_group"
+                    )
+
+
+# --- probe helper CLI -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_ENV_AUTH = re.compile(r"^\{env:([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}$")
+
+
+def describe_provider(merged: Dict[str, Any], name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """What the health probe needs about one configured provider. Never carries a secret value."""
+    prov = (merged.get("providers") or {}).get(name)
+    if not isinstance(prov, dict):
+        raise KeyError(name)
+    raw_auth = getattr(prov.get("auth"), "_raw", prov.get("auth"))
+    auth_env = None
+    if isinstance(raw_auth, str):
+        m = _ENV_AUTH.match(raw_auth.strip())
+        if m:
+            auth_env = m.group(1)
+    optin = prov.get("allow_insecure_endpoint")
+    models = prov.get("models") or {}
+    return {
+        "name": name,
+        "type": prov.get("type", "openai"),
+        "endpoint": prov.get("endpoint") or "",
+        "keyless": prov.get("keyless") is True,
+        "allow_insecure_endpoint": canonical_optin_host(optin, name) if optin is not None else None,
+        "auth_env": auth_env,
+        "cli": _is_cli_provider(prov),
+        "models": sorted(models.keys()) if isinstance(models, dict) else [],
+    }
+
+
+def _main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="endpoint_policy")
+    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
+    lp = sub.add_parser("list-providers")
+    lp.add_argument("--project-root", default=None)
+    dp = sub.add_parser("describe-provider")
+    dp.add_argument("name")
+    dp.add_argument("--project-root", default=None)
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+
+    from loa_cheval.config.loader import load_config
+
+    try:
+        merged, _sources = load_config(project_root=args.project_root)
+    except ConfigError as exc:
+        print(json.dumps({"error": "config_load_failed", "detail": str(exc)}), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 78
+    if args.cmd == "list-providers":
+        print("\n".join(sorted((merged.get("providers") or {}).keys())))
+        return 0
+    try:
+        print(json.dumps(describe_provider(merged, args.name), sort_keys=True))
+    except KeyError:
+        print(json.dumps({"error": "provider_not_configured", "provider": args.name}), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 64
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(_main())

+# --- locality (D-8.1): one classification per hop, from lib/hop-locality.py over the merged catalog + project config ----
+_ADV_LOC_TSV=""       # "<hop>\t<provider>\t<local|hosted>\t<reason>" lines, this process
+_ADV_LOC_REFUSED=""   # "<role>\t<hop>\t<provider>" lines — every hosted hop refused at plan time (the envelope names them)
+_ADV_LOC_KEPT=""      # _adv_locality_filter's answer (a global: the caller runs it at top level, never in $(...))
+_adv_locality_row() { awk -F'\t' -v h="$1" '$1 == h { print; exit }' <<<"$_ADV_LOC_TSV"; }
+_adv_locality_load() {  # <hop>... — classify the hops this process has not classified yet (one python call); fail closed
+  local -a new=(); local h line rows="" cat="${LOA_MODEL_CONFIG:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml}"
+  for h in "$@"; do [[ -n "$h" && -z "$(_adv_locality_row "$h")" ]] && new+=("$h"); done
+  (( ${#new[@]} > 0 )) || return 0
+  rows=$(python3 -I "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py" --catalog "$cat" --config "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" -- "${new[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || rows=""

+    line=$(awk -F'\t' -v h="$h" '$1 == h && NF >= 4 { print; exit }' <<<"$rows")
+    [[ -n "$line" ]] || line="${h}"$'\t'"unknown"$'\t'"hosted"$'\t'"classifier_unavailable"   # (no answer is a hosted hop)

+  done

+_adv_hop_is_local() { _adv_locality_load "$1"; [[ "$(_adv_locality_row "$1" | cut -f3)" == "local" ]]; }
+_adv_locality_filter() {  # <role> <hop>... → _ADV_LOC_KEPT: the local hops in order; each hosted one is refused by name, once per role
+  local role="$1" h p; shift
+  _ADV_LOC_KEPT=""
+  _adv_locality_load "$@"
+  for h in "$@"; do
+    [[ -n "$h" ]] || continue
+    if [[ "$(_adv_locality_row "$h" | cut -f3)" == "local" ]]; then _ADV_LOC_KEPT+="${_ADV_LOC_KEPT:+ }$h"; continue; fi
+    p=$(_adv_locality_row "$h" | cut -f2); p="${p:-unknown}"
+    if ! grep -qxF "${role}"$'\t'"${h}"$'\t'"${p}" <<<"$_ADV_LOC_REFUSED"; then
+      _ADV_LOC_REFUSED+="${role}"$'\t'"${h}"$'\t'"${p}"$'\n'

+_ADV_LOC_DEGRADED_SENTENCE="locality: local_voices — with one local family the companion is not an independent second voice (duplicate_voice, or not planned), so every security audit is DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW; adversarial-review-gate.sh and verdict-derive.sh treat this envelope exactly as they treat any other."

+_ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL=0
+_ADV_BUDGET_VOICES="[]"
+_adv_budget_estimate() {  # <estimated input tokens> <role>=<hop>... → _ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL (cents) and _ADV_BUDGET_VOICES (JSON);
+  # each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 output tokens × output rate (micro-USD per Mtok → cents: ÷ 10^10, each term
+  # truncated, as the fixed-rate formula was). An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok and is said;
+  # a zero-priced one estimates 0 and is said too.
+  local tokens="$1"; shift
+  local -a roles=() hops=() args=()
+  local rv rows="" line c_in c_out total=0 voices="[]"
+  for rv in "$@"; do roles+=("${rv%%=*}"); hops+=("${rv#*=}"); args+=(--alias "${rv#*=}"); done
+  if (( ${#hops[@]} > 0 )); then
+    rows=$(PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters" python3 -W ignore::RuntimeWarning -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing \
+      --catalog "${LOA_MODEL_CONFIG:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml}" --config "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" "${args[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || rows=""
+  fi
+  local k _bv_role _bv_hop _bv_src _bv_in _bv_out _bv_cents
+  for (( k = 0; k < ${#hops[@]}; k++ )); do
+    _bv_role="${roles[$k]}"; _bv_hop="${hops[$k]}"   # (a role word and a validated hop name — the jq operands below are small)
+    line=$(awk -v a="alias=$_bv_hop" '$1 == a { print; exit }' <<<"$rows")
+    _bv_in=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_out=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_src=$(sed -n 's/.* pricing_source=\([a-z_]*\)$/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    if [[ ! "$_bv_in" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || ! "$_bv_out" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || "$_bv_src" == "unknown" || -z "$_bv_src" ]]; then
+      _bv_in=10000000; _bv_out=30000000; _bv_src="fallback"
+      log "budget: no catalog price for $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) — the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok applies to this voice"
+    elif (( _bv_in == 0 && _bv_out == 0 )); then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c"
+    elif [[ "$_bv_src" == "stale_catalog" ]]; then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) has a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) — used as given"
+    fi
+    c_in=$(( tokens * _bv_in / 10000000000 )); c_out=$(( 2000 * _bv_out / 10000000000 )); _bv_cents=$(( c_in + c_out ))
+    total=$(( total + _bv_cents ))
+    voices=$(jq -c --arg r "$_bv_role" --arg h "$_bv_hop" --arg s "$_bv_src" --argjson c "$_bv_cents" --argjson i "$_bv_in" --argjson o "$_bv_out" \
+      '. + [{role: $r, alias: $h, estimated_cents: $c, input_per_mtok: $i, output_per_mtok: $o, pricing_source: $s}]' <<<"$voices")
+  done
+  _ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL="$total"; _ADV_BUDGET_VOICES="$voices"
+  log "budget: estimate ${total}c over ${#hops[@]} planned voice(s) ($(jq -r 'map("\(.role) \(.alias) \(.estimated_cents)c") | join(", ")' <<<"$voices"))"
+}

+  local d="$1" type="$2" sprint_id="$3" timeout="$4" diff_files="$5" alias="$6" raw="" rc=0 res="" st=""

+_adv_run_advisory_voices() {  # <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias>... — every voice started at once under
+  # $CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT seconds of wall clock for all of them; a voice still running then is killed and marked timed_out.
+  # Each voice's files are under $_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/advisory/<n>/
+  local type="$1" sprint_id="$2" timeout="$3" diff_files="$4"; shift 4

+  done
+  _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""
+  return 0

+  # `dispatch_group: local` in the merged config are planned — the primary chain here, the companion chain, the advisory
+  # voices and the KF-004 repair chain below; every hosted hop is refused by name at plan time, never rerouted. The
+  # Claude Code session model is exempt (it is the platform, not a hop of this script). Every hop is dispatched through
+  # cheval, which applies the request-time rules to a local hop (IP-literal or localhost endpoint, no DNS, redirects
+  # refused, proxy env ignored, destination in MODELINV) and records locality_mode / hop_locality from the same config key.
+  if [[ "$CONF_LOCALITY" == "invalid" ]]; then
+    error "hounfour.locality='${CONF_LOCALITY_RAW}' is neither hosted nor local_voices — nothing was planned (set hounfour.locality: hosted or local_voices)"
+    [[ "$json_output" == "true" ]] && _adv_refuse_json locality_invalid value "$CONF_LOCALITY_RAW"
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if [[ "$CONF_LOCALITY" == "local_voices" ]]; then
+    log "locality: local_voices — only hops whose provider has dispatch_group: local are planned; hosted hops are refused (the Claude Code session model is exempt)"
+    _adv_locality_filter primary "${fallback_chain[@]}"
+    if [[ -z "$_ADV_LOC_KEPT" ]]; then
+      error "locality: local_voices leaves no local hop on the primary chain (flatline_protocol.$([[ "$type" == "audit" ]] && echo security_audit || echo code_review).model / fallback_chain) — nothing was reviewed; declare a local provider (dispatch_group: local) or set hounfour.locality: hosted"

+      exit 1
+    fi
+    read -r -a fallback_chain <<<"$_ADV_LOC_KEPT"
+    model="${fallback_chain[0]}"
+    # the KF-004 repair chain is pinned to the answering voice: tiny and claude-headless are never planned (D-8.1)
+    _adv_locality_filter repair tiny claude-headless
+    [[ -n "${LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL:-}" ]] && log "WARN: locality: local_voices ignores LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL — the KF-004 repair chain is pinned to the answering voice"
+    [[ "$type" == "audit" ]] && log "$_ADV_LOC_DEGRADED_SENTENCE"
+  fi
+
+  # cycle-129 FR-7 (D-7.4, DEC-0165): advisory voices. Promotion to a counted voice is unreachable this cycle (no voice arm in
+  # run-arms.sh): an alias this block also lists in companion_chain — an attempt to count it — is refused at plan time; the
+  # hounfour.advisory_promotion knob is read and named so a later cycle adds only the arm.
+  local -a advisory_planned=()
+  if [[ -n "$CONF_ADVISORY_VOICES" ]]; then
+    local _av _ch
+    for _av in $CONF_ADVISORY_VOICES; do
+      for _ch in ${CONF_COMPANION_CHAIN_ANTHROPIC:-} ${CONF_COMPANION_CHAIN_OPENAI:-}; do
+        if [[ "$(_adv_hop_canon "$_av")" == "$(_adv_hop_canon "$_ch")" ]]; then
+          error "advisory voice ${_av} cannot be counted: no arms report line for the alias (voice arms are a future iteration)"
+          log "(hounfour.advisory_promotion: min_recall_ratio=${CONF_PROMOTION_MIN_RECALL:-unset}, max_refuted_delta=${CONF_PROMOTION_MAX_REFUTED:-unset}; remove ${_av} from companion_chain or from advisory_voices)"
+          [[ "$json_output" == "true" ]] && _adv_refuse_json advisory_promotion_refused alias "$_av"
+          exit 1
+        fi
+      done
+    done
+    if [[ "$CONF_LOCALITY" == "local_voices" ]]; then
+      # shellcheck disable=SC2086
+      _adv_locality_filter advisory $CONF_ADVISORY_VOICES
+      [[ -z "$_ADV_LOC_KEPT" ]] || read -r -a advisory_planned <<<"$_ADV_LOC_KEPT"
+    else
+      read -r -a advisory_planned <<<"$CONF_ADVISORY_VOICES"
+    fi
+  fi

+# =============================================================================
+# cycle-129 FR-7 / FR-8 (SDD D-7.4, D-7.6, D-8.1): advisory voices, the catalog-priced budget gate, locality
+# =============================================================================

+_adv_conf_advisory_voices() {  # <config key> → flatline_protocol.<key>.advisory_voices' hop names, space-separated (first
+  # occurrence kept); a non-list is said and ignored, an element that is not a hop name is said (by index and tag, never its
+  # value) and dropped — _adv_conf_chain_hops' rule. (Only the gate's own config key is spliced into the yq expressions.)
+  local config_key="$1" label="flatline_protocol.$1.advisory_voices" tg n rows="" out="" i v _nr=0
+  tg=$(yq eval ".flatline_protocol.${config_key}.advisory_voices | tag" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  [[ -z "$tg" || "$tg" == "!!null" ]] && return 0

+    [[ -n "$i" ]] || continue
+    if [[ "$tg" == ok ]]; then [[ " $out " == *" $v "* ]] || out+="$v "
+    else log "WARN: ${label}[$i] is not a hop name (${v:-unreadable}) — dropped"; fi
+  done <<<"$rows"

+# --- locality (D-8.1): one classification per hop, from lib/hop-locality.py over the merged catalog + project config ----
+_ADV_LOC_TSV=""       # "<hop>\t<provider>\t<local|hosted>\t<reason>" lines, this process
+_ADV_LOC_REFUSED=""   # "<role>\t<hop>\t<provider>" lines — every hosted hop refused at plan time (the envelope names them)
+_ADV_LOC_KEPT=""      # _adv_locality_filter's answer (a global: the caller runs it at top level, never in $(...))
+_adv_locality_row() { awk -F'\t' -v h="$1" '$1 == h { print; exit }' <<<"$_ADV_LOC_TSV"; }
+_adv_locality_load() {  # <hop>... — classify the hops this process has not classified yet (one python call); fail closed
+  local -a new=(); local h line rows="" cat="${LOA_MODEL_CONFIG:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml}"
+  for h in "$@"; do [[ -n "$h" && -z "$(_adv_locality_row "$h")" ]] && new+=("$h"); done
+  (( ${#new[@]} > 0 )) || return 0
+  rows=$(python3 -I "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py" --catalog "$cat" --config "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" -- "${new[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || rows=""
+  for h in "${new[@]}"; do
+    line=$(awk -F'\t' -v h="$h" '$1 == h && NF >= 4 { print; exit }' <<<"$rows")
+    [[ -n "$line" ]] || line="${h}"$'\t'"unknown"$'\t'"hosted"$'\t'"classifier_unavailable"   # (no answer is a hosted hop)
+    _ADV_LOC_TSV+="${line}"$'\n'
+  done
+}
+_adv_hop_is_local() { _adv_locality_load "$1"; [[ "$(_adv_locality_row "$1" | cut -f3)" == "local" ]]; }
+_adv_locality_filter() {  # <role> <hop>... → _ADV_LOC_KEPT: the local hops in order; each hosted one is refused by name, once per role
+  local role="$1" h p; shift
+  _ADV_LOC_KEPT=""

+  for h in "$@"; do
+    [[ -n "$h" ]] || continue
+    if [[ "$(_adv_locality_row "$h" | cut -f3)" == "local" ]]; then _ADV_LOC_KEPT+="${_ADV_LOC_KEPT:+ }$h"; continue; fi

+}
+# The one sentence the config comment and the audit output carry (D-8.1).
+_ADV_LOC_DEGRADED_SENTENCE="locality: local_voices — with one local family the companion is not an independent second voice (duplicate_voice, or not planned), so every security audit is DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW; adversarial-review-gate.sh and verdict-derive.sh treat this envelope exactly as they treat any other."
+
+# --- the budget gate (D-7.4, D-7.6): every planned voice at its catalog price ------------------------------------------
+_ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL=0
+_ADV_BUDGET_VOICES="[]"
+_adv_budget_estimate() {  # <estimated input tokens> <role>=<hop>... → _ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL (cents) and _ADV_BUDGET_VOICES (JSON);
+  # each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 output tokens × output rate (micro-USD per Mtok → cents: ÷ 10^10, each term
+  # truncated, as the fixed-rate formula was). An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok and is said;
+  # a zero-priced one estimates 0 and is said too.
+  local tokens="$1"; shift
+  local -a roles=() hops=() args=()
+  local rv rows="" line c_in c_out total=0 voices="[]"
+  for rv in "$@"; do roles+=("${rv%%=*}"); hops+=("${rv#*=}"); args+=(--alias "${rv#*=}"); done
+  if (( ${#hops[@]} > 0 )); then
+    rows=$(PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters" python3 -W ignore::RuntimeWarning -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing \
+      --catalog "${LOA_MODEL_CONFIG:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml}" --config "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" "${args[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || rows=""
+  fi
+  local k _bv_role _bv_hop _bv_src _bv_in _bv_out _bv_cents
+  for (( k = 0; k < ${#hops[@]}; k++ )); do
+    _bv_role="${roles[$k]}"; _bv_hop="${hops[$k]}"   # (a role word and a validated hop name — the jq operands below are small)
+    line=$(awk -v a="alias=$_bv_hop" '$1 == a { print; exit }' <<<"$rows")
+    _bv_in=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_out=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_src=$(sed -n 's/.* pricing_source=\([a-z_]*\)$/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    if [[ ! "$_bv_in" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || ! "$_bv_out" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || "$_bv_src" == "unknown" || -z "$_bv_src" ]]; then
+      _bv_in=10000000; _bv_out=30000000; _bv_src="fallback"

+    elif (( _bv_in == 0 && _bv_out == 0 )); then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c"
+    elif [[ "$_bv_src" == "stale_catalog" ]]; then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) has a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) — used as given"
+    fi
+    c_in=$(( tokens * _bv_in / 10000000000 )); c_out=$(( 2000 * _bv_out / 10000000000 )); _bv_cents=$(( c_in + c_out ))
+    total=$(( total + _bv_cents ))
+    voices=$(jq -c --arg r "$_bv_role" --arg h "$_bv_hop" --arg s "$_bv_src" --argjson c "$_bv_cents" --argjson i "$_bv_in" --argjson o "$_bv_out" \
+      '. + [{role: $r, alias: $h, estimated_cents: $c, input_per_mtok: $i, output_per_mtok: $o, pricing_source: $s}]' <<<"$voices")

+  log "budget: estimate ${total}c over ${#hops[@]} planned voice(s) ($(jq -r 'map("\(.role) \(.alias) \(.estimated_cents)c") | join(", ")' <<<"$voices"))"

+
+# --- advisory voices (D-7.4): after the counted voices, concurrently, one wall clock, findings only under advisory_voices[] ---

+_adv_advisory_walk() {  # <voice dir> <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias> — one advisory voice: the hop, then
+  # process_findings (the same schema, qualification and KF-004 repair rules as a counted voice); its rejected payloads never
+  # land beside the envelope (verdict-derive counts those), and the result is published whole
+  local d="$1" type="$2" sprint_id="$3" timeout="$4" diff_files="$5" alias="$6" raw="" rc=0 res="" st=""

+_adv_run_advisory_voices() {  # <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias>... — every voice started at once under
+  # $CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT seconds of wall clock for all of them; a voice still running then is killed and marked timed_out.
+  # Each voice's files are under $_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/advisory/<n>/
+  local type="$1" sprint_id="$2" timeout="$3" diff_files="$4"; shift 4
+  local root="$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/advisory" n=0 a d pid tok e deadline alive

+_adv_advisory_block() {  # <type> <counted result json file> <diff file> <alias>…(planned, in order) — the advisory_voices[]

+  # counted finding with the same file, overlapping lines and the same category) in config order, then every alias locality refused
+  local type="$1" counted="$2" diff_file="$3"; shift 3

+  # whole number; the envelopes travel as files)

+      res=$(cat "$d/result.json")

+        malformed_response|api_failure) st="failed"; _av_err=$(jq -r '.metadata.error // .metadata.status // ""' <<<"$res" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\037\177' | cut -c1-200) ;;
+        *) st="succeeded"; res=$(_apply_hallucination_filter "$res" "$diff_file") ;;
+      esac
+    elif [[ "$(cat "$d/status" 2>/dev/null || true)" == "prompt_copy_failed" ]]; then st="failed"; _av_err="prompt_copy_failed"
+    else st="failed"; _av_err="the voice left no result"
+    fi
+    _av_rc=$(cat "$d/rc" 2>/dev/null || echo ""); [[ "$_av_rc" =~ ^[0-9]{1,3}$ ]] || _av_rc="null"
+    printf '%s' "$res" > "$d/block-in.json"

+      --argjson rc "$_av_rc" --argjson n "$_av_n" '
+      def anc: (.anchor // "") | if type == "string" then . else "" end;
+      def file: anc | split(":")[0];

commands.name: deep-research

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator

No price is invented: this cycle adds no open-weight row, so today the invariant holds 6 vacuously and the fixture cases below prove the check itself fails when it should. 7 8 Also: the pricing module reads the provenance fields, marks a price whose `price_date` is older than 90 days as 9 `stale_catalog` (WARN, and the ledger row says so), and the `python3 -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias` CLI the 10 dissent budget gate asks prints the catalog rates or `unknown`. 11 """ 12 from __future__ import annotations 13 14 import datetime as dt 15 import json 16 import logging 17 import os 18 import re 19 import subprocess 20 import sys 21 from pathlib import Path 22 from typing import Any, Dict, List 23 24 import pytest 25 import yaml 26 27 ADAPTERS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] 28 REPO_ROOT = ADAPTERS.parents[1] 29 sys.path.insert(0, str(ADAPTERS)) 30 31 from loa_cheval.metering import pricing as pricing_mod # noqa: E402 32 from loa_cheval.metering.ledger import create_ledger_entry # noqa: E402 33 from loa_cheval.metering.pricing import ( # noqa: E402 34 STALE_PRICE_DAYS, 35 find_pricing, 36 lookup_alias, 37 price_is_stale, 38 pricing_source_for, 39 ) 40 41 CATALOG = REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "defaults" / "model-config.yaml" 42 _DATE_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$") 43 44 45 def provenance_violations(catalog: Dict[str, Any], repo_root: Path = REPO_ROOT, 46 today: dt.date | None = None) -> List[str]: 47 """Every `providers.

1	"""cycle-129 FR-7 (SDD D-7.1, D-7.2; sprint-257 Task 3.1, AC-3.1).
2	
3	Every example block in `.loa.config.yaml.example` marked `# @example-begin <name>` …
4	`# @example-end` is uncommented, merged over the System defaults with the real cheval
5	loader, and must load. The insecure-endpoint refusals (a public http host, a boolean
6	opt-in, an opt-in naming a public host, a DNS name, a link-local or metadata address,
7	a unique-local IPv6 address, a mismatched host) each fail at load with a named reason;
8	`::1`, `[::1]` and RFC1918 opt-ins are accepted when they match; one provider's opt-in
9	leaves another provider's refusals intact.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import copy
15	import re
16	import shutil
17	import sys
18	from pathlib import Path
19	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Tuple
20	
21	import pytest
22	import yaml
23	
24	sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
25	
26	from loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy import EndpointPolicyError  # noqa: E402
27	from loa_cheval.config.loader import clear_config_cache, load_config  # noqa: E402
28	from loa_cheval.types import ConfigError  # noqa: E402
29	
30	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
31	EXAMPLE = REPO_ROOT / ".loa.config.yaml.example"
32	DEFAULTS = REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "defaults" / "model-config.yaml"
33	
34	_BEGIN = re.compile(r"^#\s*@example-begin\s+([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\s*$")
35	_END = re.compile(r"^#\s*@example-end\s*$")
36	
37	
38	def extract_examples(text: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
39	    """(name, uncommented YAML) for every marked block. One leading `#` and one
40	    following space are removed per line; a nested or unterminated block fails."""
41	    blocks: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
42	    name = None
43	    lines: List[str] = []
44	    for raw in text.splitlines():
45	        if name is None:
46	            m = _BEGIN.match(raw)
47	            if m:
48	                name, lines = m.group(1), []
49	            elif _END.match(raw):
50	                raise AssertionError("@example-end without @example-begin")
51	            continue
52	        if _BEGIN.match(raw):
53	            raise AssertionError(f"nested @example-begin inside {name}")
54	        if _END.match(raw):
55	            blocks.append((name, "\n".join(lines) + "\n"))
56	            name = None
57	            continue
58	        assert raw.startswith("#"), f"example {name}: every line must be commented: {raw!r}"
59	        body = raw[1:]
60	        lines.append(body[1:] if body.startswith(" ") else body)
61	    assert name is None, f"unterminated example block {name}"
62	    return blocks
63	
64	
65	def _project(tmp_path: Path, hounfour: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
66	    root = tmp_path / "proj"
67	    (root / ".claude" / "defaults").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
68	    shutil.copy(DEFAULTS, root / ".claude" / "defaults" / "model-config.yaml")
69	    (root / ".loa.config.yaml").write_text(yaml.safe_dump({"hounfour": hounfour}, sort_keys=False))
70	    return str(root)
71	
72	
73	def _load(tmp_path: Path, hounfour: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
74	    clear_config_cache()
75	    merged, _ = load_config(project_root=_project(tmp_path, hounfour))
76	    return merged
77	
78	
79	EXAMPLES = extract_examples(EXAMPLE.read_text())
80	_BY_NAME = {n: yaml.safe_load(y)["hounfour"] for n, y in EXAMPLES}
81	
82	
83	def test_marked_examples_are_present():
84	    names = [n for n, _ in EXAMPLES]
85	    assert len(names) == len(set(names)), names
86	    for required in ("conservative", "budget-conscious", "azure-openai", "local-openai-compatible"):
87	        assert required in names, f"example {required} is not marked in {EXAMPLE.name}"
88	
89	
90	@pytest.mark.parametrize("name, body", EXAMPLES, ids=[n for n, _ in EXAMPLES])
91	def test_every_marked_example_loads(tmp_path, name, body):
92	    doc = yaml.safe_load(body)
93	    assert isinstance(doc, dict) and "hounfour" in doc, f"example {name} must be a `hounfour:` block"
94	    merged = _load(tmp_path, doc["hounfour"])
95	    for prov in (doc["hounfour"].get("providers") or {}):
96	        assert prov in merged["providers"]
97	
98	
99	def test_azure_example_carries_the_required_model_fields(tmp_path):
100	    merged = _load(tmp_path, _BY_NAME["azure-openai"])
101	    model = merged["providers"]["azure-openai"]["models"]["gpt-5-azure"]
102	    for key in ("endpoint_family", "auth_type", "dispatch_group", "context_window", "max_output_tokens"):
103	        assert model.get(key), key
104	    assert "^AZURE_OPENAI_KEY$" in merged["secret_env_allowlist"]
105	
106	
107	def test_local_example_is_keyless_local_and_opted_in(tmp_path):
108	    merged = _load(tmp_path, _BY_NAME["local-openai-compatible"])
109	    prov = merged["providers"]["local"]
110	    assert prov["keyless"] is True
111	    assert prov["allow_insecure_endpoint"] == "127.0.0.1"
112	    model = prov["models"]["qwen3-coder-30b"]
113	    assert model["dispatch_group"] == "local"
114	    assert model["streaming_recovery"] == {"first_token_deadline_s": 120}
115	    assert model["pricing"] == {"input_per_mtok": 0, "output_per_mtok": 0}
116	    assert merged["aliases"]["local-reviewer"] == "local:qwen3-coder-30b"
117	
118	
119	def test_literal_auth_local_is_normalised_to_keyless(tmp_path):
120	    cfg = copy.deepcopy(_BY_NAME["local-openai-compatible"])
121	    del cfg["providers"]["local"]["keyless"]

1	"""cycle-129 FR-7 (SDD D-7.3; sprint-257 Task 3.2, AC-3.2) — thinking traces from local
2	reasoning models on the OpenAI paths.
3	
4	* Streamed `delta.reasoning_content` deltas count as progress for the recovery tracker
5	  (they satisfy the first-token deadline) and never reach `content`; they land in
6	  `thinking`.
7	* Leading `<think>…</think>` blocks and an unterminated leading `<think>` are stripped
8	  from the content before qualification on the streaming and the non-streaming path;
9	  `thinking_stripped` is recorded in the result metadata (cheval copies it to MODELINV).
10	* The model's `streaming_recovery` block reaches the stream parser.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import json
16	import sys
17	from contextlib import contextmanager
18	from pathlib import Path
19	from typing import Any, Dict, Iterator, List

32	def _sse(*payloads: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[bytes]:
33	    return [f"data: {json.dumps(p)}\n\n".encode() for p in payloads] + [b"data: [DONE]\n\n"]

37	    return {"choices": [{"delta": delta, "finish_reason": None}], "model": "m"}

40	class _Clock:
41	    """Advances `step` seconds on every read — each SSE event costs `step` seconds."""
42	
43	    def __init__(self, step: float):
44	        self.t = 0.0
45	        self.step = step
46	
47	    def __call__(self) -> float:
48	        self.t += self.step
49	        return self.t
50

52	SLOW = {"streaming_recovery": {"first_token_deadline_s": 5}}
53	
54	
55	def test_reasoning_deltas_keep_the_tracker_alive_and_never_reach_content():
56	    chunks = _sse(
57	        _delta(reasoning_content="Let me look at the diff. "),
58	        _delta(reasoning_content="The loop is off by one. "),
59	        _delta(reasoning_content="So the finding is the bound."),
60	        _delta(content='{"findings": []}'),
61	        {"choices": [{"delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}], "model": "m"},
62	    )
63	    # every event costs 3 s against a 5 s first-token deadline: content arrives at ~15 s
64	    result = parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="local", model_data=SLOW, now_provider=_Clock(3.0))
65	    assert result.content == '{"findings": []}'
66	    assert "off by one" in (result.thinking or "")
67	    assert "Let me look" not in result.content
68	    assert result.metadata["thinking_stripped"] is True
69	    assert result.metadata["streaming_recovery"]["config_applied"]["first_token_deadline_s"] == 5.0

73	    chunks = _sse(
74	        {"choices": [], "model": "m"},     # keep-alive-shaped frames: no content, no reasoning
75	        {"choices": [], "model": "m"},
76	        {"choices": [], "model": "m"},
77	        _delta(content='{"findings": []}'),
78	    )
79	    with pytest.raises(StreamingRecoveryAbort) as info:
80	        parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="local", model_data=SLOW, now_provider=_Clock(3.0))

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""hop-locality.py — classify model hops as local or hosted for `hounfour.locality: local_voices` (cycle-129 FR-8,
+SDD D-8.0 / D-8.1, DEC-0146).
+
+    python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog <model-config.yaml> --config <.loa.config.yaml> -- <hop>...
+
+One tab-separated line per hop, in the order given:
+
+    <hop> TAB <provider|unknown> TAB <local|hosted> TAB <reason>
+
+A hop is `local` only when ALL of these hold in the merged view (the System Zone catalog overlaid with the project
+config's `hounfour.providers` / `hounfour.aliases`, the two layers cheval merges):
+  * it resolves (a `provider:id` pin, an alias chain, or a bare id that exactly one provider declares) to a model entry
+    that exists;
+  * that model entry, or its provider block, says `dispatch_group: local` (the canonical key, D-8.0);
+  * every hop on the entry's own `fallback_chain` is local by the same rule — cheval walks that chain inside one call,
+    so a local entry that falls back to a hosted one would leave the declared providers without the planner seeing it.
+Everything else is `hosted`: an unresolved hop, an unreadable config, a headless CLI hop (its dispatch group is the
+provider family's), the native session. Fail closed — a hop is never called local because it could not be read.
+
+This file reads declarations only: it never dispatches, never reads credentials and never imports the cheval package
+(run under `-I`, so neither the cwd nor PYTHONPATH reaches sys.path). The request-time rules for a local hop (IP-literal
+or localhost endpoint, no DNS, redirects refused, proxy env ignored, destination logged) are cheval's.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import sys
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+MAX_DEPTH = 10
+
+
+def _merge(base: Any, overlay: Any) -> Any:
+    if isinstance(base, dict) and isinstance(overlay, dict):
+        out = dict(base)
+        for key, value in overlay.items():
+            out[key] = _merge(base.get(key), value) if key in base else value
+        return out
+    return overlay
+
+
+def load_merged(catalog_path: str, config_path: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    import yaml
+
+    with open(catalog_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        catalog = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
+    if not isinstance(catalog, dict):
+        raise ValueError("catalog is not a mapping")
+    merged: Dict[str, Any] = {k: (catalog.get(k) if isinstance(catalog.get(k), dict) else {})
+                              for k in ("providers", "aliases", "backward_compat_aliases")}
+    if config_path:
+        try:
+            with open(config_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+                project = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            project = {}
+        if not isinstance(project, dict):
+            raise ValueError("project config is not a mapping")
+        hounfour = project.get("hounfour")
+        if isinstance(hounfour, dict):
+            for key in ("providers", "aliases"):
+                if isinstance(hounfour.get(key), dict):
+                    merged[key] = _merge(merged.get(key) or {}, hounfour[key])
+    return merged
+
+
+def _alias_target(name: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
+    for table in ("aliases", "backward_compat_aliases"):
+        target = (merged.get(table) or {}).get(name)
+        if isinstance(target, dict):
+            target = target.get("target") or target.get("model")
+        if isinstance(target, str) and target.strip():
+            return target.strip()
+    return None
+
+
+def resolve(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str]]:
+    name = (hop or "").strip()
+    if not name:
+        return None
+    current, seen = name, set()
+    for _ in range(MAX_DEPTH):
+        if ":" in current:
+            provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
+            return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
+        target = _alias_target(current, merged)
+        if not target:
+            break
+        if target in seen:
+            return None
+        seen.add(current)
+        current = target
+    if ":" in current:
+        provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
+        return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
+    providers = merged.get("providers") or {}
+    matches = [p for p, block in providers.items()
+               if isinstance(block, dict) and isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) and current in block["models"]]
+    return (matches[0], current) if len(matches) == 1 else None
+
+
+def classify(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any], _depth: int = 0, _seen: Optional[set] = None) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
+    """(provider, locality, reason) for one hop."""
+    seen = set(_seen or ())
+    target = resolve(hop, merged)
+    if target is None:
+        return "unknown", "hosted", "unresolved"
+    provider, model = target
+    block = (merged.get("providers") or {}).get(provider)
+    if not isinstance(block, dict):
+        return provider, "hosted", "provider_not_declared"
+    entry = (block.get("models") or {}).get(model) if isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) else None
+    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
+        return provider, "hosted", "model_not_declared"
+    group = entry.get("dispatch_group") or block.get("dispatch_group") or ""
+    if group != "local":
+        return provider, "hosted", f"dispatch_group={group or 'unset'}"
+    key = f"{provider}:{model}"
+    if key in seen:
+        return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"
+    seen.add(key)
+    chain = entry.get("fallback_chain") or []
+    if not isinstance(chain, list):
+        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
+    if _depth >= MAX_DEPTH:
+        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_too_deep"
+    for nxt in chain:
+        if not isinstance(nxt, str):
+            return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"

# The model-adapter shim runs cheval with its stderr discarded, so the provider's own failure line
# ("claude -p timed out after 610s") reaches only the MODELINV ledger row cheval writes for the call.
# fourth run, chunk c C-004: what travels into the tracked envelope as last_error is an allowlisted
# summary of the diagnostic — cheval's error tokens, "timed out after Ns", HTTP / exit codes —
# never the provider's raw line (request ids, account ids, echoed headers). The raw line, redacted,
----
1224:invoke_dissenter() {
invoke_dissenter() {
  local system_prompt_file="$1"
  local user_prompt_file="$2"
  local model="$3"
  local timeout="$4"
  # cycle-109 Sprint 2 T2.5 — optional sidecar path. When provided,

  # so the verdict_quality envelope lands in this file. Backward-compat:
  # callers that don't pass the arg get the legacy non-sidecar behavior.
  local vq_sidecar="${5:-}"
  # Cycle-112 D-6 (#931) — attribution type so MODELINV envelopes record
  # which phase of adversarial review (review/audit/design) issued the
  # call. Defaults empty for backward-compat with any pre-D-6 caller.
  local type="${6:-}"
  # cycle-124 FR-7: wire schema forwarded as --json-schema; cheval enforces
  # it where the hop can (Anthropic structured_json entries, claude-headless)
  # and the translated envelope reports schema_enforced either way.
  local schema_file="${7:-}"
  local -a schema_args=()
  if [[ -n "$schema_file" && -f "$schema_file" ]]; then
    schema_args=(--json-schema "$schema_file")
  elif [[ -n "$schema_file" ]]; then
    # A named schema that is not on disk means every voice runs unenforced
    # and the schema_enforced ratio is silently skewed — say so.
    log "WARN: wire schema not found, dispatching unenforced: $schema_file"
  fi
----
_adv_refuse_json() {  # <status> [key value]… → the envelope a --json caller gets when the run cannot start (it fails closed —
                      # twelfth run a3 C-004, thirteenth run a3 C-005); type / sprint_id are main's
  local st="$1"; shift
  local -a kv=(); while (( $# >= 2 )); do kv+=(--arg "$1" "$2"); shift 2; done
  jq -n --arg t "${type:-}" --arg sid "${sprint_id:-}" --arg st "$st" --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --argjson sc "$(_adv_scope_json)" ${kv[@]+"${kv[@]}"} \
    '{findings: [], metadata: ({type: $t, sprint_id: $sid, timestamp: $ts, status: $st, model: null, cost_usd: 0, scope: $sc} + ($ARGS.named | del(.t, .sid, .st, .ts, .sc)))}'   # (twenty-eighth run, a2 DISS-C-002: $ARGS.named holds --argjson bindings too)
}
_adv_scope_json() {  # [diff sha256] → metadata.scope {diff_range, diff_oids {base, head}, diff_sha256, run_tag} (nulls when absent); diff_range is main's
                     # (twenty-seventh run, a2 DISS-C-003: every envelope the script writes carries it, the refusal and the fallback record too)
  _adv_resolve_run_tag
  jq -nc --arg dr "${diff_range:-}" --arg o "${_ADV_RANGE_OIDS:-}" --arg sha "${1:-}" --arg tag "${_ADV_RUN_TAG:-}" \
    '{diff_range: (if $dr == "" then null else $dr end),
      diff_oids: (if $o == "" then null else ($o | split(" ") | {base: .[0], head: .[1]}) end),
      diff_sha256: (if $sha == "" then null else $sha end),
      run_tag: (if $tag == "" then null else $tag end)}' 2>/dev/null || printf '{"diff_range":null,"diff_oids":null,"diff_sha256":null,"run_tag":null}'
}
_adv_prev_dest_ok() {  # <path> → 0 when <path>.prev is absent or a regular file (thirty-fourth run, a4 DISS-C-002: mv into a directory, or through
                       # a link to one, moved the file INTO it, the drop's rm -f never removed it, and the skill's .prev reading met a directory)
  [[ ! -L "$1.prev" && ( ! -e "$1.prev" || -f "$1.prev" ) ]] && return 0
  error "$1.prev is not a regular file (a symlink, directory or other node — no run writes one); nothing was recorded: remove it, then run again"
  return 1
}
_adv_prev_dests_ok() {  # <path>… → 0 when every regular file among them has a .prev that is absent or a regular file — checked for ALL
----
_adv_is_same() {  # <pid> <pid=token map> → 0 while the pid is alive and still the process collected (a recorded "-": gone)
  local p="$1" e t="" now
  for e in ${2:-}; do [[ "${e%%=*}" == "$p" ]] && { t="${e#*=}"; break; }; done
  [[ "$t" == "-" ]] && return 1
  _adv_pid_alive "$p" || return 1
  if [[ -n "$t" ]]; then now=$(_adv_proc_start "$p" 2>/dev/null) || now=""; now=$(_adv_tok_word "$now"); [[ -z "$now" || "$now" == "$t" ]] || return 1; fi
  return 0
}
_ADV_REAP_TREE_TOKENS=""
_adv_reap_companion() {
  [[ -n "${_ADV_COMPANION_PID:-}" ]] || return 0
  # eighteenth run, a3 C-004: re-entered from the EXIT trap while a reap was under way — finish the kill of the tree already
  # collected instead of returning on a blank pid (the pid is cleared only once the tree has been signalled)
  if [[ "${_ADV_REAP_IN_PROGRESS:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
    # (twenty-third run, a4 DISS-C-002: before the tree is published the list holds the bare root — each pid still the process
    # collected takes its CURRENT tree with it, so a root KILLed in that window leaves no re-parented cheval / claude -p behind)
    local _x; for _x in ${_ADV_REAP_TREE_PIDS:-}; do
      if _adv_is_same "$_x" "${_ADV_REAP_TREE_TOKENS:-}"; then _adv_kill_tree "$_x" KILL >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
    done

@@ -99,6 +99,10 @@ ### Rollback (cycle-109 model)
 still `git revert` of the cycle-124 unit commits (see the Sprint 1 rollback
 proof). Env table: `grimoires/loa/runbooks/cheval-delegate-architecture.md`.
 
+cycle-129 (FR-8) — **local posture**: under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` the dissent, Flatline, Bridgebuilder and health-probe hops are planned only on providers whose model entry says `dispatch_group: local`, each hosted hop refused by name at plan time; the Claude Code session model is exempt and remains the platform, so a local posture keeps model calls local but the session itself still runs against Anthropic. Fewer voices means a DEGRADED verdict quality where the planned voice count is not met — the posture says so in the config comment and in the run output rather than inventing a voice. One fail-closed classifier (`.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py`) serves the shell scripts: an unresolved hop, an unreadable config or a local entry whose fallback chain reaches a hosted entry counts as hosted; an invalid value refuses the run.
+
+cycle-129 (FR-7) — **open-weight and local voices**: a local OpenAI-compatible server is declared as a provider (`type: openai_compat`, `keyless: true`, `allow_insecure_endpoint: "<host>"` where the host is a loopback or RFC1918 IP literal or `localhost`; Example 4 in `.loa.config.yaml.example`). The endpoint rule lives once in `.claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py` and is used by the cheval loader (`loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py`), the bash wrapper and `model-health-probe.sh --provider <name>`, which probes a configured provider's `/models` with no credential when keyless; at request time a local hop runs with no proxy, no redirects and the declared path prefix. cheval refuses an `http`, loopback or private endpoint without the opt-in at load, for every provider. On the chat-completions path a `structured_json` entry sends `response_format` json_schema and `schema_enforced` is derived from the body sent (one retry without the schema on a server 400 that names it); `reasoning_content`, `reasoning` deltas and a leading `<think>` block go to `thinking` (`thinking_stripped`); an over-window prompt is refused by name. **Advisory voices**: `flatline_protocol.code_review.advisory_voices` and `security_audit.advisory_voices` run beside the counted voices under `advisory_timeout_seconds`; their findings appear only under `advisory_voices[].findings` with `duplicate_of` links and never touch the verdict, the counts or the cost totals — promotion to a counted role needs `hounfour.advisory_promotion`. The budget gate prices each planned voice from the catalog (`loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias … --json`), whose entries now carry `open_weight`, `price_source` and `price_date`. **Bridgebuilder** reads `hounfour.providers`, `hounfour.locality` and `bridgebuilder.exit_on_degraded` from trusted configuration only (locally the working tree; on a pull request the `BRIDGEBUILDER_TRUSTED_CONFIG` repository variable, else the base branch's config, never the head), prints `completed/planned` voices and exits 3 on a DEGRADED consensus (`0` restores the old exit; `entry.sh`'s dependency preflight exits 4).
+
 ### Verification (cycle-107 sprint-1 + cycle-109 sprint-2/3 cumulative)
 
 - FL 3-model run: 549s, 3 voices' MODELINV envelopes recorded, chains populated, all primaries succeeded

+## Earned Guards and Open Voices (cycle-129)
+
+Exit codes are `0` ok, `1` refused or failed, `2` usage unless the row says otherwise. Paths are under `.claude/scripts/` unless they start with `tools/` or `evals/`.
+
+| Script | Contract | Exit codes |
+|--------|----------|------------|
+| `guard-yield.sh [--check] [--hooks-table] [--json] [--now TS] [--audit-log P] [--origins P] [--out P] [--yield-dir D] [--hooks-ref P]` | Enumerates every hook registration, `# @guard fence:<id>` and `# @guard validator:<id>` marker and gate, joins them with `.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml` and the 30-day block log (replay rows excluded; likely false positives by heuristic — never for `FR-SZ*` ids), writes the structural register `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, the host yield `.run/guard-yield.{md,json}` and the hooks-reference registration table; `--check` is the CI drift gate. | 0 ok or in sync; 1 drift; 5 a guard without an origin or an unregistered floor gate; 2 usage |
+| `run-checkpoint.sh write\|read\|derive [--json] [--write]\|record-round --gate review\|audit --file F\|mark --skill implement\|bug --sprint S\|unmark` | The run position from files: `derive` rebuilds `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` and the breaker from COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger and git (terminal and sticky states never move back); `write` derives first; `record-round` is the circuit breaker (same-issue hash, no-progress, cycle count; a trip writes OPEN and HALTED); `mark`/`unmark` manage the implementing-skill marker the implement gate reads. | 0 ok; 2 caller error (missing feedback file); 3 write failure; 4 no active cycle (callers keep the cache); 10 breaker tripped |

+- **Every guard carries its origin and its yield**: `grimoires/loa/guards.md` lists every hook, fence pattern, validator rule and gate with where it came from and whether it is active, dormant or telemetry; `.run/guard-yield.json` counts its real blocks and likely false positives over 30 days; `/loa` prints a Guards line. `guard-yield.sh --check` fails CI when a guard has no origin.
+- **Control arms**: the recall evals can run with a kernel block, the companion voice or the rule files switched off (`run-arms.sh`), against a record corpus of eight real sprints, so a rule's claim on review recall is measured before its text is cut. The kernel kept every pinned rationale this cycle (the arm run was still running at the gate) and shrank by the Agent Teams table; its byte cap fell to 9,445 B.
+- **Controls that run or go**: `implement_gate.mode` (`ask`, the default, logs a row; `telemetry`; `deny` refuses an unsanctioned App-Zone write while the run position is known), run position derived from files (`run-checkpoint.sh derive`), the circuit breaker as a script (`record-round`), per-task surgical-diff state; the input guardrails and danger-level enforcement default off in the example (82 events, zero catches), the Agent Teams rules live in their reference, and the pure-review skills carry `disallowed-tools`.
+- **The fence stops blocking prose**: a heredoc whose consumer only writes a file (`cat`, `tee`, `gh pr comment -F -`, `git commit -F -`, …) is scanned per segment, not as a command; interpreters, wrappers, substitutions, executable targets and anything unlisted still scan in full (`destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier`, corpus 99 benign / 184 dangerous rows). Two pre-existing holes closed on the way: a backtick substitution was inert to every rule, and `gh api` with a destructive method on refs, branch protection, tags, releases or the repository had no rule (`FR-GH-1`).
+- **One profile knob**: `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` sets the nine optional surfaces; no floor key is reachable through it; the example ships those keys as commented, profile-governed lines so a copied example follows the profile you choose, and `/loa` says when a guardrail control is off.
+- **Task kinds**: every sprint task says whether it is mechanical, judgment or operator work, and `tools/cycle-ratio.sh` prints the cycle's script / prose / model-call ratio.
+- **Open voices**: a local OpenAI-compatible server is a declared provider (`keyless: true`, `allow_insecure_endpoint: "127.0.0.1"`; one endpoint rule in cheval, the bash validator and `model-health-probe.sh --provider <name>`), the chat path sends `response_format` json_schema and strips thinking traces honestly, `advisory_voices` run beside the dissent's counted voices and can never change a verdict, and `hounfour.locality: local_voices` refuses every hosted hop by name across the dissent, Flatline, Bridgebuilder and the probe. Bridgebuilder reads providers only from trusted configuration, prints `completed/planned` voices and exits 3 on a degraded consensus.
+
+Upgrading: see the CHANGELOG Migration notes — `implement_gate.mode: ask` and `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: false` are the rollback keys; set `guardrails.input.enabled: true` and `guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true` (or `loa.profile: full`) to restore the old guardrail defaults.
+
 **Unreleased — decision surfaces** (cycle-128, [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)):
 
 - **Decision maps**: `/chart <slug>` maps an effort that spans more than one cycle as `question` tickets and a map doc in `grimoires/loa/maps/`. It plans and never builds, and `/plan` reports the `charting` phase.

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/adversarial-review-advisory.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.3 (PRD FR-7 AC-7.3, SDD D-7.4, DEC-0165, DEC-0155).
+#
+# Advisory voices run after the counted voices on the same prompts, concurrently, under one wall clock; their findings
+# live ONLY under advisory_voices[].findings (voice: advisory, counted_as: advisory_voice, duplicate_of links); the rest of
+# the envelope and the verdict-derive output are byte-identical (normalised: timestamps removed) with and without them;
+# a failed or timed-out advisory voice is a status, never a verdict input; an attempt to count one is refused by name.
+# Mock mode: invoke_dissenter is the harness stub (tests/unit/adversarial-review-s3-helpers.bash) — no model is called.
+# =============================================================================
+
+load adversarial-review-s3-helpers
+
+setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3adv; }   # (the CLI lock is this test's own — CMP-121)
+teardown() { s3_teardown; }
+
+_base_cfg() {  # [extra lines for the code_review block]
+    s3_config "flatline_protocol:
+  code_review:
+    enabled: true
+    model: gpt-5.5-pro
+    budget_cents: 500
+    timeout_seconds: 30
+    fallback_chain: []
+${1:-}"
+}
+
+_feedback() {  # an approved review next to the envelope, for verdict-derive
+    mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"
+    printf '%s\n' 'All good' '' 'No issues found.' \
+      '<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-x","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->' \
+      > "$OUT_DIR/engineer-feedback.md"
+}
+
+_vd() {  # → verdict-derive's --json output on the standing envelope (status recorded, output kept whatever it is)
+    "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh" --file "$OUT_DIR/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>"$T/vd.err" || true
+}
+
+@test "ADV-1 an advisory voice's findings are present only under advisory_voices[].findings, tagged and linked by duplicate_of" {
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-two]"
+    BEHAVIOUR[adv-two]=two
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json"
+    # the counted voices are untouched: primary + companion, nothing advisory at the top level
+    [ "$(jq '.findings | length' "$env")" = "2" ]
+    [ "$(jq '[.findings[] | select(.voice == "advisory")] | length' "$env")" = "0" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' "$env")" = "2" ]
+    # the block
+    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices | length' "$env")" = "1" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].alias' "$env")" = "adv-two" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].status' "$env")" = "succeeded" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].counted_as' "$env")" = "advisory_voice" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices[0].findings | length' "$env")" = "3" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '[.advisory_voices[0].findings[].voice] | unique | join(",")' "$env")" = "advisory" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '[.advisory_voices[0].findings[].id] | join(",")' "$env")" = "DISS-A1-001,DISS-A1-002,DISS-A1-003" ]
+    # same file, overlapping lines (9-12 over 10), same category → the counted primary finding; else null
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[0].duplicate_of' "$env")" = "DISS-001" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[1].duplicate_of' "$env")" = "null" ]   # (line 40: no overlap)
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[2].duplicate_of' "$env")" = "null" ]   # (same line, another category)
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[0].answered_by' "$env")" = "adv-two" ]
+    grep -qx "adv-two" "$CALLS"
+    # stdout carries the same envelope
+    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices | length' <<<"$result")" = "1" ]
+}
+
+@test "ADV-2 the envelope without advisory_voices and the verdict-derive --json output are byte-identical with and without advisory voices" {
+    _feedback
+    BEHAVIOUR[adv-two]=two; BEHAVIOUR[adv-reject]=reject; BEHAVIOUR[adv-fail]=fail
+    _base_cfg
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    cp "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" "$T/without.json"
+    _vd > "$T/vd-without.json"
+    ls "$OUT_DIR" | LC_ALL=C sort > "$T/ls-without"
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-two, adv-reject, adv-fail]"
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    cp "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" "$T/with.json"
+    _vd > "$T/vd-with.json"
+    ls "$OUT_DIR" | LC_ALL=C sort > "$T/ls-with"
+    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices | length' "$T/with.json")" = "3" ]
+    jq -e 'has("advisory_voices") | not' "$T/without.json" >/dev/null
+    # the normalised envelopes (advisory_voices deleted, timestamps removed, keys sorted) are byte-identical
+    diff <(s3_norm "$T/without.json") <(s3_norm "$T/with.json")
+    # …and each named input on its own, so a failure names it
+    local k
+    for k in '.findings' '.verdict_quality' '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' '.verdict_quality.voices_succeeded' \
+             '.metadata.companion_voice' '.metadata.rejected_summary' '.metadata.rejected_sidecars' '.metadata.cost_usd'; do
+        [ "$(jq -cS "$k" "$T/without.json")" = "$(jq -cS "$k" "$T/with.json")" ] || { echo "differs: $k"; return 1; }
+    done
+    # verdict-derive reads the same envelope and sidecars: its --json output is byte-identical
+    [ -s "$T/vd-without.json" ]
+    diff "$T/vd-without.json" "$T/vd-with.json"
+    # the advisory voice's rejected payload never landed beside the envelope (verdict-derive would count it)
+    diff "$T/ls-without" "$T/ls-with"
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[] | select(.alias == "adv-reject") | .rejected_count' "$T/with.json")" = "1" ]
+}
+
+@test "ADV-3 a failed or malformed advisory voice is recorded under advisory_voices[].status and ignored by verdict quality" {
+    BEHAVIOUR[adv-fail]=fail; BEHAVIOUR[adv-bad]=malformed
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-fail, adv-bad]"
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json"
+    [ "$(jq -r '[.advisory_voices[].status] | join(",")' "$env")" = "failed,failed" ]
+    [ "$(jq '[.advisory_voices[].findings | length] | add' "$env")" = "0" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.verdict_quality.status' "$env")" = "APPROVED" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' "$env")" = "2" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.verdict_quality.voices_succeeded' "$env")" = "2" ]
+    [ "$(jq '[.verdict_quality.voices_dropped[]?.voice] | map(select(test("adv-"))) | length' "$env")" = "0" ]
+}
+
+@test "ADV-4 the advisory wall clock is honoured: a voice still running is killed and timed_out while a fast one completes" {
+    BEHAVIOUR[adv-slow]=slow; BEHAVIOUR[adv-two]=two
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-slow, adv-two]
+    advisory_timeout_seconds: 2"
+    local t0 t1; t0=$(date +%s)
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    t1=$(date +%s)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    (( t1 - t0 < 60 ))
+    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json"
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].status' "$env")" = "timed_out" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[1].status' "$env")" = "succeeded" ]
+    grep -q "Advisory voice adv-slow: still running at the 2s advisory wall clock — killed (timed_out)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    # the hung hop did not outlive the run
+    sleep 0.5
+    ! pgrep -f "loa-s3adv-slow-$$" >/dev/null || { echo "the hung advisory hop outlived the run"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(jq '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' "$env")" = "2" ]
+}
+
+@test "ADV-5 an advisory alias the block also counts in companion_chain is refused by name at plan time, before any call" {
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [claude-headless]
+    companion_chain:
+      anthropic: [claude-headless]"
+    printf 'hounfour:\n  advisory_promotion:\n    min_recall_ratio: 0.8\n' >> "$CONFIG_FILE"
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "1" ]
+    grep -qF "advisory voice claude-headless cannot be counted: no arms report line for the alias (voice arms are a future iteration)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    grep -qF "hounfour.advisory_promotion: min_recall_ratio=0.8, max_refuted_delta=unset" "$T/stderr.log"
+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.status' <<<"$result")" = "advisory_promotion_refused" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.alias' <<<"$result")" = "claude-headless" ]
+    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
+    [ ! -e "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" ]
+}
+
+@test "ADV-6 with no advisory_voices the envelope has no advisory_voices key (the default is unchanged)" {
+    _base_cfg
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ]
+    jq -e 'has("advisory_voices") | not' "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" >/dev/null
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: []"
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    jq -e 'has("advisory_voices") | not' "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" >/dev/null
+    ! grep -q "Advisory voice" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "an empty advisory_voices ran something"; return 1; }
+}
+
+@test "ADV-7 a malformed advisory_voices value is said and ignored; a bad element is dropped by index" {
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: adv-two"
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    grep -q "advisory_voices is a str, not a list of aliases — ignored" "$T/stderr.log"
+    jq -e 'has("advisory_voices") | not' "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" >/dev/null
+    BEHAVIOUR[adv-two]=two
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-two, {x: 1}, 'bad name']"
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    grep -q "advisory_voices\[1\] is not a hop name (!!map) — dropped" "$T/stderr.log"
+    grep -q "advisory_voices\[2\] is not a hop name (!!str) — dropped" "$T/stderr.log"
+    [ "$(jq -r '[.advisory_voices[].alias] | join(",")' "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json")" = "adv-two" ]
+}
+
+@test "ADV-9 the audit gate reads security_audit.advisory_voices: the block is on adversarial-audit.json, the tally inputs unchanged" {
+    BEHAVIOUR[adv-two]=two; BEHAVIOUR[adv-reject]=reject
+    s3_config "flatline_protocol:
+  security_audit:
+    enabled: true
+    model: gpt-5.5-pro
+    budget_cents: 500
+    timeout_seconds: 30
+    fallback_chain: []
+    advisory_voices: [adv-two, adv-reject]
+  code_review:
+    advisory_voices: [not-this-gate]"
+    s3_run audit >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-audit.json"
+    [ "$(jq -r '[.advisory_voices[].alias] | join(",")' "$env")" = "adv-two,adv-reject" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[0].severity' "$env")" = "MEDIUM" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[0].duplicate_of' "$env")" = "DISS-001" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices[1].rejected_summary | length' "$env")" = "1" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.rejected_count' "$env")" = "0" ]
+    ! grep -qx "not-this-gate" "$CALLS" || { echo "the review block's advisory voice ran on the audit gate"; return 1; }
+}
+
+@test "ADV-8 the review and audit skills tell the reader to read advisory_voices[].findings as advisory input" {
+    grep -q 'advisory_voices\[\]\.findings' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"

+++ b/tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget.bats
